sn2.1:1.3: The commentary says that godlings (_devaputta_) are born “in the lap of the gods”, that is, not from a womb. Typically, in contrast with the “deities” (_devatā_), they are named individuals. The commentary also takes the term as gendered, with _devaputta_ as “son of god” and _devadhītā_ as “daughter of god”, but as the latter term is not attested in early Pali (or Sanskrit) we should probably take _devaputta_ as gender-neutral (like _devatā_). In early Sanskrit, indeed, we only find _devaputra_ as an adjective, “the heaven and earth, whose children are gods”; at Rig Veda 1.185.4 those children are “two young women, sisters”.
sn2.1:2.1: I read _sikkhetha_ as second person plural optative, and _subhāsitassa_ (etc.) as dative (of purpose), although we would expect the _āya_ form in this sense. The commentary glosses with third singular and accusative (_subhāsitaṁ sikkheyya_). Norman (*Elders Verses I*, note 239) suggests it may be locative.
